entities.title: Session
entities.summary: One Engine and its State: everything one `afs serve` or `afs jsonl` process remembers, or a single `afs call`.
notToBeConfusedWith: An MCP client's conversation, which may restart afs and so start a new session

entities.title: Etag
entities.summary: `b3:` and the first 64 bits of a BLAKE3 hash in hex: of a file's bytes for read, stat and diff_since, or of the reply value for search, list and outline.
notToBeConfusedWith: Stamp: file metadata, compared without reading the file

entities.title: Stamp
entities.summary: A file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime (in nanoseconds), the Ident type; equal stamps outside the racy window are taken to mean unchanged content.

entities.title: Racy window
entities.summary: The 2 seconds after a file's mtime or ctime during which its stamp proves nothing; the term comes from git.

entities.title: Ref
entities.summary: r1, r2, …: the session's id for a reply that carried content; an unchanged marker names the ref of the reply that holds the content.

entities.title: Unchanged marker
entities.summary: A reply {etag, unchanged: true, ref} sent instead of content the session already sent for the same request shape.
notToBeConfusedWith: cached: true, which says the result was reused from the cache but is still sent in full

entities.title: Hunk
entities.summary: One change in a diff reply: at (1-based old line), del (old lines removed), new_at (1-based new line) and ins (the new text, absent for a pure deletion).

entities.title: Diff base
entities.summary: A version of a file whose bytes the session holds and that it sent in full, so a later whole-file read can be answered with hunks.
notToBeConfusedWith: Any version diff_since can use: diff_since accepts every held version, complete or not

entities.title: Walk configuration
entities.summary: A search's paths, globs, hidden and no_ignore together; a session keeps one trigram index per walk configuration.

entities.title: Trigram
entities.summary: Three consecutive bytes folded to ASCII lower case and packed into one number; the index maps each to the files containing it.

entities.title: Plan
entities.summary: The prefilter derived from a pattern: sets of trigrams, one per literal every match must start (or end) with; a file is a candidate when it has every trigram of at least one set.

entities.title: Always-scan file
entities.summary: A file the index never filters out: over 2 MiB, inside the racy window when read, or unreadable; every indexed search scans it.
